findings.text: blocking: the Query double at :20-34 computes the expected answer itself (missing = (stage != superseded or not retired_is_exempt) and sources == 0 and not (origin == 'derived' and children)) and returns rows on that basis, so require_producing_sources is only ever asked whether it raises on a pre-decided row list. The production predicate at imas_codex/standard_names/source_invariant.py:44-49 is never executed by this test: deleting the superseded exemption or the whole AND NOT (derived-parent) clause leaves it green, so four of the done_when's invariant cases (derived parent passes, retired name passes, one source passes, none raises) are simulated rather than asserted. Put the regression back by removing AND NOT ({_derived_parent_cypher()}) from source_invariant.py:48 and the test does not redden; assert against the Cypher the invariant builds, or against a double that evaluates the emitted predicate, so the classification is verifiable.

follow-on: the in-transaction branch added at graph_ops.py:5508-5528 (and its twin at imas_codex/standard_names/attachment_audit.py:1086-1103) is selected only when type(gc) is GraphClient, but every test in the covering selection hands in a MagicMock, a FakeGraph or a _ScopedClient, so the branch never executes in any recorded arm. The only production caller passing a real client, attachment_audit.py:2767 and provenance_rebuild.py:531, therefore has its new transactional path, and its rollback on refusal, landed without a gate; the node's own evidence page concedes the doubles route on query text and do not evaluate Cypher.

follow-on: _is_sourceless_name is production code with no production caller; the only importer is the node's own test at tests/standard_names/test_writers_carry_sources.py:10. It mirrors the Cypher predicate a second time, so the rule that a live non-derived name needs a producer now has two implementations which can drift silently, and its docstring scopes it to small fixtures, which is a test concern living in a source module.

follow-on: _find_orphaned_names already answers the same question with WHERE NOT (:StandardNameSource)-[:PRODUCED_NAME]->(sn) over an explicit id list, and the new owner module re-implements that predicate instead of the helper being folded onto it; two sourceless-name queries now coexist in the same package, so a future change to what counts as sourced must be made in both.
